title: get_max_l1_space() misses HYBRID per-core allocations, so ttnn CB budgets can overestimate free L1
body:
## Summary

`ttnn::operations::data_movement::get_max_l1_space()` budgets CBs against `device->lowest_occupied_compute_l1_address()`, which in HYBRID allocator mode does not see per-core allocations on cores other than bank 0, nor any that live on a per-device rather than the mesh allocator. `ProgramImpl::validate_circular_buffer_region()` *does* see them. Ops budgeting with the helper can therefore build a CB plan the validator then rejects.

## Detail

The per-bank query is HYBRID-aware (`tt_metal/impl/allocator/allocator.cpp:425-439`): it also checks `AllocatorID{bank_id + 1}`, the bank's per-core allocator. But the device-level query only ever asks about bank 0, on the default sub-device manager's allocator:

```cpp
// tt_metal/impl/sub_device/sub_device_manager_tracker.cpp:160
constexpr uint32_t global_bank_id = 0;
const auto& global_allocator = default_sub_device_manager_->allocator(SubDeviceId{0});
auto found_addr = global_allocator->get_lowest_occupied_l1_address(global_bank_id);
```

The validator, in HYBRID mode, discards that value and walks every core in each CB's core range across every physical device allocator (`tt_metal/impl/program/program.cpp:1895-1911`), precisely because per-core allocations can land at different addresses per core and can live on per-device allocators.

So the two disagree in exactly the configuration per-core allocation exists to support: `experimental_set_per_core_allocation` on a core other than bank 0's.

## Affected callers

`get_max_l1_space()` / `is_enough_space()` in `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/data_movement/common/common.cpp:432`, reached from at least:

- `untilize` (native, via `enough_space_height`; and the codegen program factory as of #53399)
- `transpose`
- `matmul_utilities`
- `reshard_rm_program_factory`

Ops that place work over the full compute-with-storage grid are maximally exposed, since every core is in some CB's range.

## Suggested fix

Expose one frontier helper in the allocator layer that is allocator-mode-aware and takes a core range, and have both `validate_circular_buffer_region()` and the ttnn helpers call it. That removes the class of divergence rather than patching one caller.

Note the cost asymmetry when scheduling this: the precise frontier is an O(cores) walk. That is fine once per program-cache miss, which is where every current ttnn caller sits. It would not be fine on a per-dispatch path.

## Context

Raised as a suppressed comment in the Copilot review on #53399. Pre-existing — that PR tightens the codegen budget from whole-of-L1 to this helper's frontier, which is a strict improvement but inherits the blind spot.

Related: #53399
